follow-up time: Duration of phototherapy and 8 hours after phototherapy
study type: Single-center parallel randomized controlled open-label trial
outcome: Side effects (skin rash, diarrhoea, increased body temperature)
cohort: 104 newborns ≥ 34 weeks' gestation who received phototherapy for indirect hyperbilirubinemia
finding: Intermittent phototherapy (IPT) was found to be as effective as continuous phototherapy (CPT) in reducing total serum bilirubin, with a shorter duration of therapy, slower rebound bilirubin rate, shorter hospital stays, and lower incidence of side effects.
mod_finding: This study found no significant differences between the mode of delivery for infants receiving intermittent vs. continuous phototherapy.
